resolution.what_changed: All six devices instrumented, each its own measured pass (bus, sudo_relay by Akien's ruling that the common discipline is the default, ground_loop, tester, trouble, web_server — see each evidence row's disposition). Every pass: real crossings identified (never a blanket sprinkle), thin per-crossing breadcrumbs, a tooth pinning exactly-these-crumbs, netns-sealed, clean under the build gate. The whole-repo build_inspector sweep now reads CLEAN — zero findings — and the gate at the emit-chokepoint holds the line for every future build. A recurrence is a NEW ticket at count 1 pointing at this fix (the lane's own rule).

the_trouble: SIX BaseDevice subclasses inherit emit() and never call self.emit() outside proofs: bus, ground_loop, sudo_relay, tester, trouble, web_server. MAP.md:434 (2026-07-14): 'Every major state transition and every interface boundary is logged (base reflex, inherited)... no device can opt out.' A device CAN currently opt out by simply not calling — the base gives the capability, nothing makes the crossing use it. The bus is the sharpest instance: it is the boundary the logging standard names FIRST, and it is silent at every crossing.
why_it_matters: Law 7 — a silent device fails invisibly (the system_rackmount went-red-silently gap, systemic). Also the exact history: 'i have been resigned to the fact that we wouldn't have such logging until some lever presented itself' (Akien, 2026-07-27) — this ticket is the lever's first pull.

evidence.the_homonym: relay.py:234 calls a module-level audit function NAMED emit — a genuine audit record, not the DiagnosticBase surface; the original word-scoped measure counted it and this component passed the sweep on it

evidence.why_it_matters: Law 7 + MAP.md:434, AND the measuring lesson: the first sweep's measure counted any call of the word 'emit'; sudo_relay passed on a homonym (its module-level audit emit) and harbor_master's transitions.emit chokepoint call would have covered a device there too. The census now checks the receiver (self.emit) — words-kept-meanings-replaced, caught in the instrument itself. Disposition for sudo_relay is the OWNER's: its audit trail is real, deliberate instrumentation — the question is whether its device surface should ALSO breadcrumb its crossings, or whether its charter answers 'it doesn't, because the audit record IS the crossing log' (a valid answer under learning-as-a-pattern; silence is not).
evidence.disposition: DISPOSED 2026-07-27, by Akien's ruling: 'why is the obvious answer of it should use the same logging as everything else not assumed to be the case?' — the question above had the burden inverted. The common discipline is the DEFAULT; deviation carries the argument, and there was none: the audit record and the device breadcrumb are Law 7's two different kinds (record of truth vs diagnostic), so the audit trail never answered for the device surface — the 'it doesn't, because X' clause is for components with genuinely no crossings, not for components that log through a private second door. Applied: request_root emits one breadcrumb per round-trip (pointer=audit record id, values={returncode}, after the round-trip lands); reads emit nothing; the module-level audit writer is RENAMED emit → write_audit, removing the homonym at its source. Tooth: test_the_crossing_is_no_longer_silent (real round-trip via a one-iteration daemon thread). 9/9 green, netns-sealed, clean under the gate.

disposition_note: NOT fixed in the discovery turn, deliberately: instrumenting a device's crossings means identifying its real gates (which transitions, which boundaries), per component — measured work, not a sed pass. A blanket emit() sprinkled to green the filter would be the hollow build (Law 8). Each becomes its own instrumentation pass; the filter holds the line meanwhile.
